title: Grid recovery funding can be large while disbursement, completion, and stability remain limited
source_unit: U.S. Government Accountability Office GAO-26-107772 review of federal support for Puerto Rico electricity-grid recovery and modernization since 2017
geography: Puerto Rico; FEMA, HUD, DOE, PREPA, COR3, LUMA Energy, Genera PR, and approximately 1.5 million grid customers

denominator.unit: federal obligations and disbursements for Puerto Rico grid recovery; agency and project denominators differ

total_obligated.unit: billion dollars obligated by FEMA, HUD, and DOE since 2017

fema_disbursed.unit: billion dollars disbursed from FEMA obligations

other_agency_obligations.value: HUD about $2.3 billion; DOE about $937 million

solar_funds_reallocated_or_canceled.unit: million dollars originally for community and low-income household solar projects

observations.method: GAO review of federal and Puerto Rico documents and data, agency interviews, a site visit, and interviews with officials, contractors, and operators.
observations.uncertainty: Obligations and disbursements do not establish usable service, household bill effects, reliability, project completion, or equitable access; agency accounting and project stages differ.
observations.subgroup: Puerto Rico grid recovery and modernization, including FEMA, HUD, and DOE programs and selected utility operators.
observations.counterinterpretation: Slow disbursement can reflect reimbursement rules, project sequencing, review requirements, or prudent controls rather than waste; some funded capacity may be valuable before final completion.

observations.period: As of February 2026; project and vegetation-clearing realization

denominator.unit: miles of transmission and distribution lines planned for vegetation clearing

clearance_share.unit: percent of planned miles cleared, calculated from reported 400 and 16000

grid_stability.value: limited progress in key areas; outages had become more frequent, including an almost two-day total blackout in April 2025

observations.method: GAO comparison of planned and completed project information, stakeholder reports, and documented outage and recovery context.
observations.uncertainty: The mileage comparison does not measure all grid work or reliability causes; nine completed projects are not a completion rate for the full portfolio and outage frequency is not attributed to one project or agency.
observations.subgroup: Transmission and distribution vegetation management and selected large FEMA projects.
observations.counterinterpretation: Clearing miles is only one part of grid stability; generation, transmission, finance, operations, fuel, weather, and maintenance can matter independently.

denominator.unit: GAO recommendations to FEMA and DOE on guidance, staffing, roles, and coordination

implementation_barriers.value: project review processes, staff turnover, complex funding, PREPA's financial condition, and uncertainty among recovery entities

coordination_gap.value: a formal coordination mechanism including all relevant Puerto Rico and federal entities did not exist

recommendation_status.value: FEMA and DOE agreed with the recommendations; implementation remains open

observations.method: GAO assessment of program roles, guidance, review processes, staffing, financial conditions, and interagency coordination.
observations.uncertainty: A documented coordination gap does not by itself establish the size of the delay or a causal effect on any customer's outage, bill, health, business, or political judgment.
observations.subgroup: Federal agencies, Puerto Rico entities, PREPA, grid operators, contractors, and recovery stakeholders.
observations.counterinterpretation: Multiple agencies and operators can provide useful specialization; adding a formal mechanism may improve clarity without guaranteeing faster or more reliable service.

related_sources.claim: Official full GAO report provides the project, funding, disbursement, operating, and coordination detail behind this bounded record.
Earlier GAO review supplies historical context on Puerto Rico grid recovery and coordination; this record does not pool its older estimates with the 2026 figures.

boundary: This record identifies a conversion gap between federal obligations, disbursement, project completion, grid operations, and household electricity stability. It does not establish a same-customer outage, bill, health, business, migration, trust, or political-action outcome, and it does not attribute all grid conditions to federal implementation.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official GAO product page used for extracted aggregate and bounded progress figures; full report is linked but not retained in this record.
